/entries/e_maria/desc: The Marquesa de Montemayor lives in Lima and writes letters to sustain her bond with her distant daughter.
/entries/e_maria/archive/0/fields/0/text: A cloth merchant’s daughter, married at twenty-six to an impoverished nobleman
/entries/e_maria/archive/0/fields/2/text: Her story to the actress about her daughter holding her face comes from a recurring dream
/entries/e_maria/archive/0/fields/3/text: At the inn she writes anew, trying to stop demanding proof of her daughter’s love
/entries/e_maria/archive/1/fields/1/text: She made a mountain pilgrimage for her daughter’s confinement and took the bridge on the return to Lima
/entries/e_maria/archive/1/fields/2/text: The letter she calls her first is the one later preserved as Letter LVI
/entries/e_maria/archive/1/fields/3/text: Her surviving words were understood later than the eccentric figure she made in the streets
/entries/e_clara/desc: María’s clever, self-possessed daughter moves to Spain after marriage. She also gives generously to people around her.
/entries/e_clara/archive/0/fields/1/text: Faced with her mother’s endless concern, she increasingly uses distance to preserve a life of her own
/entries/e_clara/archive/0/fields/2/text: She generously helps friends, servants and artists; her coldness is not equally directed at everyone
/entries/e_clara/archive/0/fields/3/text: She mentions her pregnancy lightly, provoking still greater anxiety in her mother
/entries/e_pepita/desc: A girl brought up at the convent and sent to keep the Marquesa company, trying to meet expectations beyond her years.
/entries/e_pepita/archive/0/fields/1/tex: Trained as the abbess’s successor, she is used to fulfilling her duty before considering herself
/entries/e_pepita/archive/0/fields/2/tex: She resists the servants’ theft and bullying while enduring her mistress’s wavering attention
/entries/e_pepita/archive/0/fields/3/tex: She hopes to return for a few days, or to receive even a short letter she can keep
/entries/e_abbess/desc: The head of the Convent of Santa Rosa cares for the sick and orphaned, works for women’s dignity, and anxiously seeks a successor.
/entries/e_abbess/archive/0/fields/0/tex: Women protecting one another and caring for orphans, the sick and women without support
/entries/e_abbess/archive/0/fields/3/tex: Beside the laundry trough, she saw the child organize the work while vividly telling a saint’s story
/entries/e_abbess/archive/0/fields/4/tex: Being trusted as an adult made the girl proud, but afraid to reveal that she might not be capable
/entries/e_abbess/archive/1/fields/0/tex: She asks the surviving young man to come inside and help, recalling things he once did for her
/entries/e_abbess/archive/1/fields/1/lab: The young man who slips away
/entries/e_abbess/archive/1/fields/2/lab: Whom she later asks for help
/entries/e_abbess/archive/1/fields/3/tex: Twice calling him her friend and moving nearer still makes him flee; she does not stop seeking another way
/entries/e_abbess/archive/1/fields/4/tex: She admits she too has lost someone; the young man remembers those words
/entries/e_abbess/archive/2/fields/0/tex: He promises to put his house in order and ask the abbess to find someone to manage it
/entries/e_abbess/archive/2/fields/1/lab: The child he hopes to educate
/entries/e_abbess/archive/2/fields/2/lab: The child’s home before the proposed move
/entries/e_abbess/archive/2/fields/3/tex: These are still promises Pio makes to obtain consent, not care arrangements already carried out
/entries/e_abbess/archive/2/fields/4/tex: The rooms, patients and food she manages make care more than a kindly word
/entries/e_camila/desc: A café singer who becomes the celebrated actress La Perichole, seeking a life among art, love, respectability and motherhood.
/entries/e_camila/archive/0/fields/0/tex: She can put an aristocrat’s private affairs into an improvised song and swiftly sway the whole audience
/entries/e_camila/archive/0/fields/3/tex: She thinks the Marquesa deliberately forgives the insult; in fact, her listener hardly heard the songs
/entries/e_camila/archive/0/fields/4/tex: She spends a long time before the mirror, unable to mock the woman as easily as before
/entries/e_camila/archive/1/title: Letters others must not know about
/entries/e_camila/archive/1/fields/1/lab: The writing she entrusts to him
/entries/e_camila/archive/1/fields/2/tex: Pio normally reads and writes for her, but she deliberately keeps these private exchanges from him
/entries/e_camila/archive/1/fields/3/tex: She pays after each letter, reminding the copyist that this closeness is still hired work
/entries/e_camila/archive/1/fields/4/tex: Disappointed over an appointment, she comes to the brothers’ room, unaware how a witness understands their whispers
/entries/e_camila/archive/2/title: A mother and an old companion
/entries/e_camila/archive/2/fields/1/lab: The little object she gives her son before departure
/entries/e_camila/archive/2/fields/2/tex: A desire for social standing, but also weariness with the roles, insults and exhausting work
/entries/e_camila/archive/2/fields/3/tex: After her illness she refuses visitors and expressly forbids Pio the estate; his care does not erase that boundary
/entries/e_camila/archive/2/fields/4/tex: Before agreeing to a year’s education, she insists that the child be asked whether he wishes to go
/entries/e_pio/desc: Called Uncle without being a relative, this worldly wanderer and theatre mentor mixes love of talent with a wish to control others.
/entries/e_pio/archive/0/fields/2/text: Teaching, reading, writing, hairdressing, errands and accounts: much of the work unheard in the applause
/entries/e_pio/archive/0/fields/3/text: An affectionate social title, not evidence of a blood relationship with the actress
/entries/e_pio/archive/0/fields/4/text: In writing about the actress, the Marquesa also mentions the man so often beside her
/entries/e_pio/archive/1/fields/1/label: The object present at his intrusion
/entries/e_pio/archive/1/fields/2/text: He sincerely loves literature and craft, yet often hurts his pupil through mockery, silence and withheld praise
/entries/e_pio/archive/1/fields/3/text: Refused permission to educate the child, he pressures her with a debt; withdrawing the demand cannot undo its hurt
/entries/e_pio/archive/1/fields/4/text: Noticing that the jolting cart makes the child ill, he carries him on his shoulder instead
